intro: Hanoi rewards visitors with layered history, buzzing streets and remarkable food. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro Line 2A runs Cat Linh to Yen Nghia; Line 3 runs Cau Giay to Nhon.
Metro fares are distance-based, about 8,000-15,000 VND; tap contactless cards at gates.
City buses are cheap and air-conditioned, about 7,000-12,000 VND per ride.
Grab works well for cars and motorbike taxis; fares are fixed in the app.
Metered taxis: Mai Linh and Taxi Group are reliable; flag-fall about 20,000 VND.
Traffic is chaotic; walking is fine in the Old Quarter but crossing takes nerve.

mausoleum.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
mausoleum.hours: Tue–Thu and Sat–Sun, morning only; closed Mon and Fri. Check exact times on the day.
mausoleum.tip: Dress modestly, keep quiet and leave bags and cameras outside. Queues are long, so arrive early.

oldquarter.name: Hanoi Old Quarter
oldquarter.hours: Always open; liveliest in the evening
oldquarter.tip: Walk the '36 streets' slowly and look up at the old tube houses. Cross roads at a steady pace.

templeliterature.name: Temple of Literature
templeliterature.price_text: ≈ VND 70,000 adult; check on the day
templeliterature.tip: Vietnam's first university. Go early to avoid tour groups and heat.

citadel.name: Imperial Citadel of Thang Long
citadel.tip: Large site with few crowds. Allow time for the underground bunkers and the flag tower.

onepillar.name: One Pillar Pagoda
onepillar.tip: Small and quick. Combine it with the mausoleum and museum in one morning.

cathedral.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
cathedral.hours: Exterior always visible; interior only around mass times
cathedral.tip: Best seen from the café terraces opposite. Check mass times before going inside.

hoankiem.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
hoankiem.tip: Walk the loop at dawn to see locals exercising, or on weekend evenings when cars are banned.

dongxuan.name: Dong Xuan Market
dongxuan.price_text: Free to enter; pay per item
dongxuan.hours: Daily roughly 06:00–18:00; night market Fri–Sun evening
dongxuan.tip: Go for the wholesale halls and the weekend night market. Bargain politely.

opera.name: Hanoi Opera House
opera.price_text: Ticket price varies by performance; check on the day
opera.hours: Performances mostly evening; exterior viewable daily
opera.tip: Book tickets ahead if you want a show. Otherwise see the French colonial facade at night.

trainstreet.name: Hanoi Train Street
trainstreet.hours: Access is often restricted; check on the day
trainstreet.tip: Rules change often and parts are closed to visitors. Never stand on the tracks.

mydinh.name: My Dinh National Stadium
mydinh.price_text: Match tickets vary; check on the day
mydinh.hours: Open on event days; check schedule
mydinh.tip: Only worth the trip for a football match or concert. It is far from the centre.

ngocson.name: Ngoc Son Temple
ngocson.tip: Cross the red Huc Bridge for lake views and the temple on its island.

pho.name: Pho (Hanoi noodle soup)
pho.hours: Most pho shops open early morning and close by early afternoon
pho.tip: Hanoi pho is clear broth with beef. Try a busy local stall early in the morning.

redriver.name: Red River
redriver.tip: See the river from Long Bien Bridge at sunrise. Walk carefully on the old bridge.

longbien.name: Long Bien Bridge walk
longbien.tip: Historic bridge over the Red River. Stay on the pedestrian side and watch for motorbikes.

streetfoodtour.name: Old Quarter street food tour
streetfoodtour.price_text: ≈ VND 500,000–900,000 per person; check on the day
streetfoodtour.hours: Tours usually run late afternoon and evening
streetfoodtour.tip: A guided walk is the easiest way to try bun cha, banh cuon and egg coffee. Confirm what is included.

waterpuppet.name: Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre
waterpuppet.price_text: ≈ VND 100,000–200,000 by seat; check on the day
waterpuppet.hours: Several shows daily, mostly afternoon and evening
waterpuppet.tip: A short, family-friendly show near Hoan Kiem Lake. Book ahead for front seats.

westlake.name: West Lake (Tay Ho) walk
westlake.tip: Quieter lakeside loop with cafés and temples. Good for a sunset walk away from the crowds.

dongxuanfood.name: Dong Xuan night food stalls
dongxuanfood.tip: Cheap local snacks in the weekend night market. Bring small notes.

frenchquarter.name: French Quarter walk
frenchquarter.tip: Wide boulevards and colonial buildings around the Opera House. Best in the cooler morning.

eggcoffee.name: Egg coffee café stop
eggcoffee.tip: Hanoi's sweet egg coffee is a must-try. Many cafés hide up narrow staircases.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Temples, the Old Quarter lanes and water puppets.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Pho, bun cha and street-side coffee crawls.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum, Hoa Lo and museums.

stays.why: Walk to Hoan Kiem Lake, street food and markets. Lively and loud; ask for a quiet room.
Wide tree-lined streets, the Opera House and quieter nights, a short walk from the lake.
Central and handy for the lake, the Old Quarter edge and evening walks.
Lakeside expat area with cafés and quieter streets; 15–25 minutes by taxi to the centre.

food: Start with pho for breakfast, bun cha at lunch and a bia hoi (fresh beer) corner in the evening.
Eat where locals sit: small stalls and family restaurants in the Old Quarter are often the best value.
Try egg coffee (ca phe trung) and strong drip coffee at a café near Hoan Kiem Lake.
Street food is cheap: expect roughly 30,000–80,000 VND for a bowl or plate; check on the day.
Drink bottled water and eat busy, freshly cooked stalls. Carry small notes for street vendors.
more_time: Swap a city day for Ha Long Bay or Lan Ha Bay: a long day trip or an overnight on a boat.
Take a half-day to the Temple of Literature and the Imperial Citadel if you like history.
Spend an afternoon in Tay Ho for lakeside cafés and a quieter side of Hanoi.
